messages.author: 5cd8214ff6863dcf
messages.subject: Minloadcrit - Autocalibration in GGIR
parts:
Hello everyone,

I have a question about auto calibration in GGIR. What is the minimum number of hours the code needs to read for the auto calibration procedure to be effective? In the reference paper and in the sample code you have 72 hours. Can we use one-day data in our pilot testing?

Is 24 hours of data sufficient to minimize calibration error under 0.01 g?


Thanks,

Charu

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Minloadcrit - Autocalibration in GGIR
parts:
Success of autocalibration depends on availability of sufficient non-movement periods and whether the lack of calibration during the first day(s) of recording is representative for the rest of the recording. If the person wore the sensor during the first day of measurement, then auto-calibration should get enough non-movement data points to do its work.

Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
https://accelting.com/
